research_question: How much safety can route-local operation-fit thresholds recover while retaining the accepted-selector endpoint-accuracy gain, without changing models or execution authority?
architecture: Keep the accepted operation-fit selector from PR #190.
Keep candidate recall, candidate-fit, BGE scorer, endpoint descriptions, and endpoint-disambiguation configuration unchanged.
Set the global operation-fit min score to 0.0 and apply preregistered per-route min-score maps.
Thresholds affect only already-registered operation IDs and cannot create routes or authority.
No calibration, blind, or consumed predecessor rows are used.

candidate_maps.name: dev-safety-budget-12
candidate_maps.objective: maximize development supported top-route retention subject to <=12 unsupported false accepts in the top-score heuristic

candidate_maps.name: production-safety-budget-6
candidate_maps.objective: maximize development supported top-route retention subject to <=6 unsupported false accepts in the top-score heuristic

evaluation.note: Threshold derivation and evaluation both use tuning-eligible development evidence; resulting metrics are development selection evidence and require fresh calibration after freeze.

interpretation_rule: This is a scalar route-local safety baseline. Even if safety gates pass, failure to reach the supported-accuracy gate means the architecture is diagnostic-only and motivates typed negative/unknown multi-view evidence rather than further calibration on consumed data.
